faq.a: Rahela is associated with the Arabic form رَاحِيلَة, whose core sense is rahela; rachel (south asian form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Rahela?
faq.a: Rahela is associated with Arabic. Rahela is a South Asian form of Arabic رَاحِيل (Rāḥīl), the name Rachel.
Yes — the underlying form رَاحِيلَة is Arabic.
Rahela can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Rahela should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Rāḥīl is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Rahela mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Rahela is rendered راحیلہ and carries the sense راحیلہ، حضرت راحیل.

faq.q: What does Rahela mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Rahela is rendered راحله and carries the sense راحله، راحیل.
A romanized syllable approximation is ra-he-la. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Rahela?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Rahela, rahela. Script forms are راحله, راحيله, راحیلہ, رَاحِيلَة, राहेला.

faq.q: Is Rahela a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
